# Improve the staged experiment

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a snapshot you may repair: inspect its
source, effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic,
logs, tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an
unusual setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed
behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health.

## Your job

If you find a defect, fix it in the staged workspace at `/workspace`. **Do not
launch training.** Do not start the experiment, in the foreground or
background, and do not use `nohup`, `&`, `tmux`, `screen`, or any detach
mechanism. The system runs the experiment itself after you finish (see below);
mechanism. The system runs the experiment itself after you finish (see below);
anything you launch is wasted and scores nothing. Cheap, non-training checks
are fine.

When you are done, submit a report at `/workspace/report.md`. It must
summarize:

1. **Root cause** — the defect you found, and the evidence in the workspace
   (logs, metrics, code) that connects it to the observed behavior.
2. **Changes** — every file you changed and what you changed in it.
3. **Expected effect** — which metric the fix should move and in which
   direction.

A missing or empty `/workspace/report.md` scores 0.

## What the system will run

After you submit the report, the system deletes everything under
`$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, then re-runs the experiment in your
repaired workspace as a foreground process, using the launch script:

```text
examples/retool/retool_qwen3_4b_rl.sh
```

with this environment:

```text
LOG_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs
WANDB_MODE=offline
WANDB_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs
```

The effective run must use:

- HF checkpoint `/workspace/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft`
- Megatron torch_dist reference `/workspace/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft_torch_dist`
- train data `/workspace/zhuzilin_dapo-math-17k/dapo-math-17k.jsonl`
- validation data `/workspace/zhuzilin_aime-2024/aime-2024.jsonl`
- `--num-rollout 70`
- `--eval-interval 10`

**Make sure your repaired launch script actually produces that run.** The
staged `examples/retool/retool_qwen3_4b_rl.sh` bakes `--num-rollout 3000`
directly into the training invocation with no environment override, and the
graded rerun passes no budget override either — if you leave 3000 in place,
the rerun blows its time budget and scores 0. Edit the script to the required
70.

Four more traps specific to this task:

- **Log placement is your script's job.** The launch script builds the Ray
  runtime-env JSON itself and only propagates a few variables into the
  training process — `WANDB_DIR` set in the environment does **not** reach it.
  Your repaired script must itself write the training log and the offline
  W&B data under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` (offline W&B below
  `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs/wandb`), or the grader will find no
  metrics to grade.
- **The W&B key.** The script passes `--wandb-key ${WANDB_API_KEY}` unquoted;
  offline mode gets a harmless local placeholder from the environment, so the
  script must not choke when it is a placeholder rather than a real key.
- **Read-only scoring assets.** The exact-match scorer
  `slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_dapo_utils.py`, the tool sandbox
  `examples/retool/tool_sandbox.py`, and the staged datasets
  `zhuzilin_dapo-math-17k/` and `zhuzilin_aime-2024/` are verified correct and
  graded read-only: after the rerun the verifier hashes them, and any
  modification, replacement, or deletion scores 0 no matter what the metrics
  say. The length-term repair belongs in the reward function in
  `examples/retool/generate_with_retool.py` — remove the injected term, do not
  re-tune the scoring around it.
- **The launch script's scoring and eval wiring is fixed.** Beyond the
  instructed `--num-rollout 70` edit and the log-placement repair, the script
  must keep wiring the run exactly as staged: the custom generate/reward-manager
  paths (`generate_with_retool.generate` /
  `generate_with_retool.reward_func`), the eval on `aime` over the staged
  `aime-2024.jsonl`, `--eval-interval 10`, `--n-samples-per-eval-prompt 16`,
  `--eval-max-response-len 16384`, and `--eval-top-p 1`. The verifier checks
  these after the rerun; repointing the scorer, swapping the eval dataset, or
  resampling evals scores 0 no matter what the metrics say.

A task-specific grading script then reads **only this fresh run's** files
under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` and scores the key metrics; logs
written anywhere else are ignored. Do not copy, edit, or fabricate log
metrics. Otherwise the run is scored 0.
I'll start by exploring the staged workspace to understand the experiment structure.

35	DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-$PWD}

40	TRAIN_DATA_DIR=${TRAIN_DATA_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/zhuzilin_dapo-math-17k}

45	# Download the training set if it is not already present under DATA_DIR.
46	if [ ! -f "$TRAIN_DATA" ]; then
47	   echo "[data] $TRAIN_DATA missing; downloading zhuzilin/dapo-math-17k from $HF_ENDPOINT"
48	   hf download --repo-type dataset zhuzilin/dapo-math-17k --local-dir "$TRAIN_DATA_DIR"
49	fi
50	
51	# Download the eval set if it is not already present under DATA_DIR.
52	if [ ! -f "$EVAL_DATA" ]; then
53	   echo "[data] $EVAL_DATA missing; downloading zhuzilin/aime-2024 from $HF_ENDPOINT"
54	   hf download --repo-type dataset zhuzilin/aime-2024 --local-dir "$EVAL_DATA_DIR"
55	fi
56	
57	# --- model checkpoints -----------------------------------------------------
58	# The SFT'd HF checkpoint and its mcore (torch_dist) conversion used as ref weights.
59	HF_MODEL_DIR=${HF_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft}
60	DIST_MODEL_DIR=${DIST_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft_torch_dist}
61	
62	# Download the HF checkpoint if it is not already present under MODEL_DIR.
63	if [ ! -d "$HF_MODEL_DIR" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A "$HF_MODEL_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
64	   echo "[model] $HF_MODEL_DIR missing; downloading font-info/qwen3-4b-sft-SGLang-RL from $HF_ENDPOINT"
65	   hf download font-info/qwen3-4b-sft-SGLang-RL --local-dir "$HF_MODEL_DIR"
66	fi
67	
68	# Convert to a torch_dist (mcore) checkpoint if not already done.
69	if [ ! -d "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
70	   echo "[model] converting $HF_MODEL_DIR -> $DIST_MODEL_DIR (torch_dist)"
71	   PYTHONPATH=${MEGATRON_LM_DIR:-/root/Megatron-LM} python "${SLIME_DIR}/tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py" \
72	      "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
73	      --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR" \
74	      --rotary-base 5000000 \
75	      --save "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"
76	fi
77	
78	# Where training checkpoints go. This must NOT live under $HF_MODEL_DIR: that

#!/bin/bash

# for rerun the task
pkill -9 sglang
sleep 3
ray stop --force
pkill -9 ray
pkill -9 python
sleep 3
pkill -9 ray
pkill -9 python

set -ex

# will prevent ray from buffering stdout/stderr
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

NVLINK_COUNT=$(nvidia-smi topo -m 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'NV[0-9][0-9]*' | wc -l)
if [ "$NVLINK_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    HAS_NVLINK=1
else
    HAS_NVLINK=0
fi
echo "HAS_NVLINK: $HAS_NVLINK (detected $NVLINK_COUNT NVLink references)"

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"
# slime repo root (this recipe lives at <slime>/examples/retool)
SLIME_DIR="$(cd -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." &>/dev/null && pwd)"
source "${SLIME_DIR}/scripts/models/qwen3-4B.sh"

# Use the HuggingFace mirror for all downloads.
export HF_ENDPOINT=${HF_ENDPOINT:-https://hf-mirror.com}

# Root locations for data and models; default to $PWD, override via env.
DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-$PWD}
MODEL_DIR=${MODEL_DIR:-$PWD}

# --- datasets --------------------------------------------------------------
# Training set (DAPO-Math-17k) and eval set (AIME-2024), pulled from the Hub.
TRAIN_DATA_DIR=${TRAIN_DATA_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/zhuzilin_dapo-math-17k}
EVAL_DATA_DIR=${EVAL_DATA_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/zhuzilin_aime-2024}
TRAIN_DATA=${TRAIN_DATA:-$TRAIN_DATA_DIR/dapo-math-17k.jsonl}
EVAL_DATA=${EVAL_DATA:-$EVAL_DATA_DIR/aime-2024.jsonl}

# Download the training set if it is not already present under DATA_DIR.
if [ ! -f "$TRAIN_DATA" ]; then
   echo "[data] $TRAIN_DATA missing; downloading zhuzilin/dapo-math-17k from $HF_ENDPOINT"
   hf download --repo-type dataset zhuzilin/dapo-math-17k --local-dir "$TRAIN_DATA_DIR"
fi

# Download the eval set if it is not already present under DATA_DIR.
if [ ! -f "$EVAL_DATA" ]; then
   echo "[data] $EVAL_DATA missing; downloading zhuzilin/aime-2024 from $HF_ENDPOINT"
   hf download --repo-type dataset zhuzilin/aime-2024 --local-dir "$EVAL_DATA_DIR"
fi

# --- model checkpoints -----------------------------------------------------
# The SFT'd HF checkpoint and its mcore (torch_dist) conversion used as ref weights.
HF_MODEL_DIR=${HF_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft}
DIST_MODEL_DIR=${DIST_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft_torch_dist}

# Download the HF checkpoint if it is not already present under MODEL_DIR.
if [ ! -d "$HF_MODEL_DIR" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A "$HF_MODEL_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
   echo "[model] $HF_MODEL_DIR missing; downloading font-info/qwen3-4b-sft-SGLang-RL from $HF_ENDPOINT"
   hf download font-info/qwen3-4b-sft-SGLang-RL --local-dir "$HF_MODEL_DIR"
fi

# Convert to a torch_dist (mcore) checkpoint if not already done.
if [ ! -d "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
   echo "[model] converting $HF_MODEL_DIR -> $DIST_MODEL_DIR (torch_dist)"
   PYTHONPATH=${MEGATRON_LM_DIR:-/root/Megatron-LM} python "${SLIME_DIR}/tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py" \
      "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
      --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR" \
      --rotary-base 5000000 \
      --save "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"
fi

# Where training checkpoints go. This must NOT live under $HF_MODEL_DIR: that
# directory is the input checkpoint and may be mounted read-only, in which case
# --save would fail partway through the first save interval rather than at
# startup. Default keeps the old directory name, just under a writable root.
OUTPUT_DIR=${OUTPUT_DIR:-$PWD/outputs}

CKPT_ARGS=(
   --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR"
   --ref-load "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"
   # --load "$MODEL_DIR/Qwen3-4B_slime/"
   --save "$OUTPUT_DIR/qwen3-4b-sft-multi-turn/"
   --save-interval 10
   --rotary-base 5000000
)

ROLLOUT_ARGS=(
   --prompt-data "$TRAIN_DATA"
   --input-key prompt
   --label-key label
   --apply-chat-template
   --rollout-shuffle
   --reward-key score
   --num-rollout 3000
   --rollout-batch-size 32
   --n-samples-per-prompt 8
   --rollout-max-context-len 16384
   --rollout-max-response-len 16384
   --rollout-temperature 1

   --global-batch-size 256
   --balance-data
)

EVAL_ARGS=(
   --eval-interval 10
   --eval-prompt-data aime  "$EVAL_DATA"
   --n-samples-per-eval-prompt 16
   --eval-max-response-len 16384
   --eval-top-p 1
)

PERF_ARGS=(
   --tensor-model-parallel-size 2
   --sequence-parallel
   --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1
   --context-parallel-size 1
   --expert-model-parallel-size 1
   --expert-tensor-parallel-size 1

   --recompute-granularity full
   --recompute-method uniform
   --recompute-num-layers 1

   # --micro-batch-size 1
   --use-dynamic-batch-size
   --max-tokens-per-gpu 9216
)

GRPO_ARGS=(
   --advantage-estimator grpo
   --use-kl-loss
   --kl-loss-coef 0.00
   --kl-loss-type low_var_kl
   --entropy-coef 0.00
   --eps-clip 0.2
   --eps-clip-high 0.28
)

OPTIMIZER_ARGS=(
   --optimizer adam
   --lr 1e-6
   --lr-decay-style constant
   --weight-decay 0.1
   --adam-beta1 0.9
   --adam-beta2 0.98
)

WANDB_ARGS=(
   --use-wandb
   --wandb-project slime-retool
   --wandb-group qwen3-4B-retool-multi-turn
   --wandb-key ${WANDB_API_KEY}
)

SGLANG_ARGS=(
   --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine 2
   --sglang-mem-fraction-static 0.7
   --sglang-server-concurrency 128
   # 让 router 自己扛过 ~1s 抖动，客户端就不会看到 500
   --router-retry-max-retries 8
   --router-retry-initial-backoff-ms 200
   --router-retry-max-backoff-ms 3000
   --router-retry-backoff-multiplier 1.5
   # colocate 突发下熔断弊大于利
   --router-disable-circuit-breaker
)

MISC_ARGS=(
   # default dropout in megatron is 0.1
   --attention-dropout 0.0
   --hidden-dropout 0.0
   # should be good for model performance
   --accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32
   --attention-softmax-in-fp32
   # need to comment this when using model with MLA
   --attention-backend flash
)

CUSTOM_ARGS=(
   --custom-generate-function-path generate_with_retool.generate
   --custom-rm-path generate_with_retool.reward_func
)

# launch the master node of ray in container
export MASTER_ADDR=${MASTER_ADDR:-"127.0.0.1"}
ray start --head --node-ip-address ${MASTER_ADDR} --num-gpus 8 --disable-usage-stats --dashboard-host=0.0.0.0 --dashboard-port=8265

# Build the runtime environment JSON with proper variable substitution
RUNTIME_ENV_JSON="{
  \"env_vars\": {
    \"PYTHONPATH\": \"${MEGATRON_LM_DIR:-/root/Megatron-LM}/:${SCRIPT_DIR}:${SLIME_DIR}\",
    \"CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS\": \"1\",
    \"NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE\": \"${HAS_NVLINK}\"
  }
}"

ray job submit --address="http://127.0.0.1:8265" \
   --runtime-env-json="${RUNTIME_ENV_JSON}" \
   -- python3 train.py \
   --actor-num-nodes 1 \
   --actor-num-gpus-per-node 8 \
   --colocate \
   ${MODEL_ARGS[@]} \
   ${CKPT_ARGS[@]} \
   ${ROLLOUT_ARGS[@]} \
   ${OPTIMIZER_ARGS[@]} \
   ${GRPO_ARGS[@]} \
   ${WANDB_ARGS[@]} \
   ${PERF_ARGS[@]} \
   ${EVAL_ARGS[@]} \
   ${SGLANG_ARGS[@]} \
   ${MISC_ARGS[@]} \
   ${CUSTOM_ARGS[@]}

import re
import signal


def last_boxed_only_string(string: str) -> str | None:
    """Extract the last LaTeX boxed expression from a string.

    Args:
        string: Input string containing LaTeX code

    Returns:
        The last boxed expression or None if not found
    """
    idx = string.rfind("\\boxed{")
    if idx < 0:
        return None

    i = idx
    right_brace_idx = None
    num_left_braces_open = 0

    while i < len(string):
        if string[i] == "{":
            num_left_braces_open += 1
        if string[i] == "}":
            num_left_braces_open -= 1
            if num_left_braces_open == 0:
                right_brace_idx = i
                break
        i += 1

    return string[idx : right_brace_idx + 1] if right_brace_idx is not None else None


def remove_boxed(s: str) -> str:
    """Remove the LaTeX boxed command from a string.

    Args:
        s: String with format "\\boxed{content}"

    Returns:
        The content inside the boxed command
    """
    left = "\\boxed{"
    assert s[: len(left)] == left, f"box error: {s}"
    assert s[-1] == "}", f"box error: {s}"
    return s[len(left) : -1]

    def __enter__(self):
        signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, self.handle_timeout)
        signal.alarm(self.seconds)

    def __exit__(self, type, value, traceback):
        signal.alarm(0)

def last_boxed_only_string(string: str) -> str | None:
    """Extract the last LaTeX boxed expression from a string.

    Args:
        string: Input string containing LaTeX code

    Returns:
        The last boxed expression or None if not found
    """
    idx = string.rfind("\\boxed{")
    if idx < 0:
        return None

    i = idx
    right_brace_idx = None
    num_left_braces_open = 0

    while i < len(string):
        if string[i] == "{":
            num_left_braces_open += 1
        if string[i] == "}":
            num_left_braces_open -= 1
            if num_left_braces_open == 0:
                right_brace_idx = i
                break
        i += 1

    return string[idx : right_brace_idx + 1] if right_brace_idx is not None else None


def remove_boxed(s: str) -> str:
    """Remove the LaTeX boxed command from a string.

    Args:
        s: String with format "\\boxed{content}"

    Returns:
        The content inside the boxed command
    """
    left = "\\boxed{"
    assert s[: len(left)] == left, f"box error: {s}"
    assert s[-1] == "}", f"box error: {s}"
    return s[len(left) : -1]


class timeout:

    def __init__(self, seconds=1, error_message="Timeout"):
        self.seconds = seconds
        self.error_message = error_message

    def handle_timeout(self, signum, frame):
        raise TimeoutError(self.error_message)

    def __enter__(self):
        signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, self.handle_timeout)
        signal.alarm(self.seconds)

    def __exit__(self, type, value, traceback):
        signal.alarm(0)

@trace_function("generate_and_rm", target="sample")
async def generate_and_rm(
    args: Namespace,
    sample: Sample | list[Sample],
    sampling_params: dict[str, Any],
    evaluation: bool = False,
) -> Sample | list[Sample]:
    # mask previous off-policy generation for partial rollout
    if args.partial_rollout and args.mask_offpolicy_in_partial_rollout and sample.response_length > 0:
        sample.loss_mask = [0] * sample.response_length

    # For samples with existing response, check if they're complete
    if sample.status == Sample.Status.COMPLETED or sample.status == Sample.Status.TRUNCATED:
        assert sample.response is not None
        if not args.group_rm:
            assert sample.reward is not None
        return sample

    state = GenerateState(args)

    # generate
    async with state.semaphore:
        if state.aborted:
            sample.status = Sample.Status.ABORTED
            return sample

        with state.dp_rank_context() as _:
            # Check sample.generate_function_path for per-sample custom_generate_function_path (e.g., from eval dataset config)
            custom_func_path = getattr(sample, "generate_function_path", None) or args.custom_generate_function_path

            if custom_func_path is not None:
                custom_generate_func = load_function(custom_func_path)
                # if signature has evaluation, pass evaluation
                if "evaluation" in inspect.signature(custom_generate_func).parameters:
                    sample = await custom_generate_func(args, sample, sampling_params, evaluation=evaluation)
                else:
                    sample = await custom_generate_func(args, sample, sampling_params)
            else:
                sample = await generate(args, sample, sampling_params)

    sample = await apply_rollout_sample_hooks(args, sample, evaluation=evaluation)

    # for the rm that need the whole group, we will not do the rm here
    if args.group_rm:
        return sample

    if isinstance(sample, list):
        samples = sample
        if any(sample.status == Sample.Status.ABORTED for sample in samples):
            return samples

        samples_need_reward = [sample for sample in samples if sample.reward is None]
        with trace_span(samples_need_reward, "reward_model"):
            rewards = await batched_async_rm(args, samples_need_reward)
        for sample, reward in zip(samples_need_reward, rewards, strict=False):
            sample.reward = reward
        return samples
    else:
        if sample.status == Sample.Status.ABORTED:
            return sample
        # Some custom generate paths may have already filled the reward.
        if sample.reward is None:
            with trace_span(sample, "reward_model"):
                sample.reward = await async_rm(args, sample)

    return sample

    # ``generate_and_rm`` may return either a ``Sample`` or a ``list[Sample]``

    for sample in group:

async def generate_and_rm(
    args: Namespace,
    sample: Sample | list[Sample],
    sampling_params: dict[str, Any],
    evaluation: bool = False,
) -> Sample | list[Sample]:
    # mask previous off-policy generation for partial rollout
    if args.partial_rollout and args.mask_offpolicy_in_partial_rollout and sample.response_length > 0:
        sample.loss_mask = [0] * sample.response_length

    # For samples with existing response, check if they're complete
    if sample.status == Sample.Status.COMPLETED or sample.status == Sample.Status.TRUNCATED:
        assert sample.response is not None
        if not args.group_rm:
            assert sample.reward is not None
        return sample

    state = GenerateState(args)

    # generate
    async with state.semaphore:
        if state.aborted:
            sample.status = Sample.Status.ABORTED
            return sample

        with state.dp_rank_context() as _:
            # Check sample.generate_function_path for per-sample custom_generate_function_path (e.g., from eval dataset config)
            custom_func_path = getattr(sample, "generate_function_path", None) or args.custom_generate_function_path

            if custom_func_path is not None:
                custom_generate_func = load_function(custom_func_path)
                # if signature has evaluation, pass evaluation
                if "evaluation" in inspect.signature(custom_generate_func).parameters:
                    sample = await custom_generate_func(args, sample, sampling_params, evaluation=evaluation)
                else:
                    sample = await custom_generate_func(args, sample, sampling_params)
            else:
                sample = await generate(args, sample, sampling_params)

    sample = await apply_rollout_sample_hooks(args, sample, evaluation=evaluation)

    # for the rm that need the whole group, we will not do the rm here
    if args.group_rm:
        return sample

    if isinstance(sample, list):
        samples = sample
        if any(sample.status == Sample.Status.ABORTED for sample in samples):
            return samples

        samples_need_reward = [sample for sample in samples if sample.reward is None]
        with trace_span(samples_need_reward, "reward_model"):
            rewards = await batched_async_rm(args, samples_need_reward)
        for sample, reward in zip(samples_need_reward, rewards, strict=False):
            sample.reward = reward
        return samples
    else:
        if sample.status == Sample.Status.ABORTED:
            return sample
        # Some custom generate paths may have already filled the reward.
        if sample.reward is None:
            with trace_span(sample, "reward_model"):
                sample.reward = await async_rm(args, sample)

    return sample

) -> float:
    """Compute the reward score for a solution.

    Args:
        solution_str: The solution string
        ground_truth: The ground truth answer
        config: Configuration object containing reward model settings
        pause_tokens_index: Indices of pause tokens

    Returns:
        Reward score (1.0 for correct, -1.0 for incorrect)
    """
    # Limit solution length for efficiency
    solution_str = solution_str[-300:]  # The longest answer in MATH-500 has 159 characters

    # Verify the solution
    correct, pred = verify(solution_str, ground_truth, strict_box_verify, pause_tokens_index)

    reward = 1.0 if correct else -1.0
    acc = correct

    return {
        "score": reward,
        "acc": acc,
        "pred": pred,
    }

fi

arguments.content:
# Repair report — `slime_retool` post-training experiment

## 1. Root cause

The reward function injected an **unbounded length-inflation term** directly into the
score returned to both training and held-out evaluation, causing classic reward
hacking: the policy learned to maximize response *length* (including rambling to the
16,384-token cap), not answer *correctness*.

Defect in `examples/retool/generate_with_retool.py` (`reward_func`), now removed:

```python
length_ratio = min(sample.response_length / args.rollout_max_response_len, 1.0)
result["score"] = result["score"] + 5 * length_ratio
```

The base `math_dapo_compute_score` returns **±1** (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_dapo_utils.py`
`compute_score`). Adding `+5·(len/16384)` swamps it: any response of ≳3,277 tokens is
scored positive **even when the answer is wrong**, and a response that hits the 16k
truncation cap earns ≈+4–5 regardless of correctness. Every token of extra length is
positively rewarded.

### Evidence connecting defect → observed behavior (frozen run, `outputs/metrics.json` + `wandb/offline-run-20261104_233821-wz5z4fp9/files/output.log`)

The held-out metric `eval/aime` is defined as the **mean of this same `reward_func`
score** over AIME-2024 (eval goes through `--custom-rm-path generate_with_retool.reward_func`;
see `slime/ray/rollout.py` `_log_eval_rollout_data`: `eval/{key} = mean(rewards)`). So the
injected term inflates the graded metric itself:

| eval step | eval/aime | eval/aime/response_len/mean | eval/aime/truncated_ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0  | 0.356 | 3,916  | 0.8%  |
| 19 | 0.470 | 4,251  | 1.0%  |
| 39 | 1.094 | 6,294  | 4.2%  |
| 49 | 1.743 | 8,238  | 13.5% |
| 59 | 2.543 | 10,846 | 31.3% |
| 69 | 3.014 | 12,394 | 47.3% |

The three series move in lockstep: `eval/aime` climbs 0.36 → 3.01 **while** eval response
length triples (3.9k → 12.4k) and the truncated fraction explodes 0.8% → 47.3%. By step 69
almost half the eval samples are truncated at the 16k cap — responses that mostly *cannot*
contain a correct final `Answer: \boxed{...}` — yet the metric is at its peak. A genuine

All repairs complete and verified. Summary of what I found and fixed:

## Diagnosis

The experiment was **unhealthy** — a reward-hacking failure. `reward_func` in `examples/retool/generate_with_retool.py` injected an unbounded length bonus (`+5 × response_length/16384`) on top of the ±1 exact-match score. Since that bonus overwhelms the correctness signal (any response over ~3.3k tokens scores positive *even when wrong*), the policy learned to maximize length instead of accuracy.

The frozen evidence ties the defect directly to observed behavior: `eval/aime` (defined as the mean of this same reward) climbed **0.36 → 3.01** in lockstep with eval response length (**3.9k → 12.4k tokens**) and truncation ratio (**0.8% → 47.3%**). A true accuracy is bounded in [−1, 1] — a value of 3.01 while half the eval samples hit the 16k cap is proof the metric was being gamed by length, not earned by correctness.

## Fixes (3 files staged, no training launched)

1. **`generate_with_retool.py`** — removed the two-line injected length term. Reward is now exact-match (±1) plus the original small tool-shaping term. Verified: a 16k-token wrong response now scores **−0.95** (was ≈+4.05); correct answers score exactly 1.0 at any length.

2. **`retool_qwen3_4b_rl.sh`** — (a) `--num-rollout 3000 → 70` as required; (b) fixed log placement so the graded rerun actually writes under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`: the Ray runtime env only propagates listed vars, so I added `WANDB_MODE`/`WANDB_DIR=$LOG_DIR`/`WANDB_SILENT` to `RUNTIME_ENV_JSON`, added `--wandb-dir "$LOG_DIR"`, and piped the driver log through `tee "$LOG_DIR/train.log"`. All other wiring (scorer path, AIME eval data, `--eval-interval 10`, sampling, model/data paths) left untouched.

3. **`/workspace/report.md`** — full root-cause / changes / expected-effect writeup.

The read-only scoring assets (`math_dapo_utils.py`, `tool_sandbox.py`, both datasets) were verified untouched. The fixed run should report `eval/aime` as a genuine accuracy in [−1, 1], with eval response length and truncation collapsing back from their hacked runaway.
